newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli police detain Jews in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israeli police detain Jews in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli security forces in Hebron detained nearly 20 Jewish settlers who tried to take over houses in the Arab casbah of the West Bank town early on Tuesday, Israeli army radio and witnesses said.
The settlers oppose an imminent deal with Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority to give self-rule to 80 percent of Hebron, a town holy to Jews and Moslems as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.
The radio said about 20 people were arrested, most of them before dawn. Witnesess saw police detain five of them who had raised an Israeli flag and held morning prayers in a vacant house.

Arafat said earlier he hoped to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday to close the deal on an Israeli troop pullback in Hebron, the last of seven West Bank Arab towns due to be given autonomy under a 1995 self-rule accord.

The settlers accuse Netanyahu, the right-wing Likud party leader opposed to swapping occupied land for peace with the Arabs, of betraying them by sticking to the U.S.-backed deal signed by the left-centre government he ousted in May.
Soldiers clashed with settlers last week after a similar pre-dawn takeover of two vacant houses. The settlers say they want to take back houses that once belonged to Jews.

"Those houses that belong to Jews and are under Israeli control must be inhabited, given Israeli control and thus they will be returned to their owners," Tsuriel Popovich, a settler leader, told the radio.
"We intended to enter them, settle in them and in the meantime the security forces arrived and halted the whole story," he said after the first roundup of settlers.
About 400 Jewish settlers, the Tomb of the Patriarchs and about 20,000 of Hebron's 100,000 Palestinians, including the casbah, are in the 20 percent of the town due to remain under Israeli control.
Officials say the deal could be implemented within a week of an agreement.
